items.evidence: Repository and editorial facts map to F1-F6 and official sources S1-S5.
I1-I2 and D1-D3 clearly separate derivative workflows from existing Remotion capabilities.
GitHub ID, repository identity, license, state, fetch time, and raw counters match the snapshot.
Uncertainty is explicit; dynamic counters are snapshots and proposed features are not presented as existing facts.
The hook uses Remotion's distinctive code-to-video model.
The summary covers data-driven templates, code-controlled composition, and rendered video output.
React composition, code control, and batch rendering are evidenced core capabilities.
React, TypeScript, and FFmpeg are retained at an appropriate product-understanding level.
The hook creates a memory point while the summary alone carries the complete product explanation.
The summary describes the original project; meaning discusses why its verified capabilities are reusable.
Each opportunity connects code/batch capabilities or code friction to a focused interface opportunity.
Project audience, direction audiences, complete approaches, and 3-6 item scopes remain separate.
All three directions name a concrete user and a recurring problem.
All three directions state input, core workflow, and visible outcome in the page copy and rationale.
Every direction names the Remotion capability it reuses and changes audience, workflow, or outcome.
Each direction has a closed 3-4 item first-version scope that supports the stated flow.
Short-form scripts, article knowledge cards, and product fields differ in input, workflow, and output.
Every direction names a concrete burden reduced or experience created rather than generic efficiency.
At least one direction primarily serves personal, family, learning, or creative value.
